//: Canonical destructive-command rule table for both cluster repos. This file is the single source of truth: .claude/hooks/guard-destructive.sh and .opencode/plugins/guard-destructive.js are GENERATED from it by gen-guards.py, so the bash and JS guards cannot drift apart. Patterns are written in the intersection of POSIX ERE (grep -E) and JavaScript RegExp so one string serves both.

always_allow.//: Read-only validation is never blocked, whatever else the command matches.

rules.alternative: Use 'just kube apply-ks <ns> <ks>' to apply changes via Flux

rules.exempt_reason: PVC recreation (miroir StorageClass migrations, restore drills) is routine and always paired with a verified kopiur snapshot. The marker opts a single command out of THIS rule only -- every other rule, including talosctl reset/wipe, still applies. See .agents/skills/recreate-pvc/SKILL.md.
rules.alternative: Confirm with the user before deleting cluster resources. If this is a planned PVC recreation with a verified snapshot, append the marker documented in .agents/skills/recreate-pvc/SKILL.md

rules.reason: Direct helm mutations are not allowed — config lives in HelmRelease manifests
rules.alternative: Edit the HelmRelease values and apply via Flux
Confirm with the user before deleting Flux resources

rules.reason: talosctl patch machineconfig duplicates array fields (machine.files etc.) and can brick the node
rules.alternative: Use 'just talos apply-node <node>' or talosctl apply-config --file for full config replacement

rules.reason: talosctl patch machineconfig duplicates array fields (machine.files etc.) and can brick the node
rules.alternative: Use a minimal DELTA patch file, or 'talosctl apply-config --file' for a full replacement — never pass talos/patches/controlplane.yaml, it is a gen-time patch and will strand the node

rules.reason: talosctl reset/wipe is destructive and irreversible
rules.alternative: Confirm explicitly with the user before proceeding

rules.reason: Frostlink is a single node — talosctl upgrade/reboot/shutdown is a FULL cluster outage with nothing to fail over to
rules.alternative: Use 'just talos upgrade <version>' (it resolves the schematic first), and only with the user watching

rules.reason: Recursive delete on a sensitive path
rules.alternative: Confirm the exact path with the user before deleting

rules.reason: mv REPLACES a mise-managed symlink with a regular file, silently unlinking it from ~/dotfiles — edits then stop reaching the repo
rules.alternative: Use `cp` instead of `mv`, which writes through the symlink and keeps it intact
